rfm_tuples.claim_text: FY2025 10-K records a $931.5M goodwill impairment across all five reporting units (Canalys $42.7M, NetLine $34.7M, Bluefin Legacy $174.1M, Industry Dive $243.4M, legacy TechTarget $436.7M). Goodwill fell from $973.4M to $45.6M YoY. The company also incurred a net loss of approximately $1.0B in fiscal 2025. Q1 2026 10-Q follows with an additional $45M impairment, wiping out Canalys ($8.1M), Bluefin ($3.7M), NetLine ($6.8M) completely; post-reorg B2D segment goodwill also fully impaired.
rfm_tuples.R: We recorded an impairment charge of $931.5 million related to the goodwill in all reporting units... we incurred losses of $1.0 billion driven mainly by non-cash charges for impairment of goodwill
rfm_tuples.f_method: internal_consistency — purchase-price test on the Dec 2024 reverse merger (Informa Tech Digital Businesses contributed to public TTGT shell); reconcile $931.5M FY25 + $45M Q1-26 = $976M cumulative impairment against the originally-recorded purchase consideration
rfm_tuples.M_source: 10-K Note 6 (Goodwill) + Q1 2026 10-Q Note 4 + reporting-unit allocation table
rfm_tuples.M_value: Gross carrying amount of goodwill at 3/31/2026 = $1,183.6M; accumulated impairment = $1,182.5M = 99.9% of all goodwill ever recorded has been written off within 15 months of the Dec 2, 2024 merger close. Legacy TechTarget reporting unit (the original public co that Informa acquired for $350M cash + stock) was impaired to $0 in FY2025. Industry Dive was impaired $243.4M (carrying $25.7M post-impairment vs presumably ~$269M pre); Bluefin Legacy fully impaired to $0 by Q1 2026. PwC issued a critical audit matter specifically on the goodwill impairment assessments.
rfm_tuples.interpretation: Mode B: a ~$1.0B impairment representing ~99.9% of recorded goodwill within 15 months of closing the December 2024 reverse merger is a forensic indictment of the deal itself. Either (a) the purchase price was unsupportable from day one (M&A overpayment by Informa PLC at the expense of legacy TTGT public shareholders) or (b) the underlying assets deteriorated catastrophically in <12 months. Both interpretations point to an issuer whose central capital-allocation act of 2024 has been retroactively repudiated by its own audit committee. Q1 2026 continued impairment ($45M more) means the bleeding has not stopped at the FY2025 cutoff.

rfm_tuples.claim_text: 10-K Item 9A: 'Our principal executive officer and principal financial officer concluded that our disclosure controls and procedures were not effective as of December 31, 2025, due to the material weaknesses in our internal control over financial reporting... As of the date hereof, our material weaknesses, as described in Item 9A, have not been remediated.' Multiple material weaknesses identified (control environment, period-end financial reporting, non-routine transactions, IT general controls) that already caused restatement of FY2023 financial statements and all 2023/2024 interim periods, plus immaterial misstatements to substantially all significant accounts in 2024 and 2025.
rfm_tuples.R: Our management previously identified the following material weaknesses... and such material weaknesses remain unremediated as of December 31, 2025... insufficient segregation of duties... did not design and maintain effective controls over the period-end financial reporting process... resulted in the restatement of the Company's financial statements as of December 31, 2023
rfm_tuples.f_method: audit_trail — verify PwC's audit opinion explicitly carves out an adverse opinion on internal controls; check that material weaknesses are not first-disclosure but persisting from prior year(s)
rfm_tuples.M_source: 10-K Item 9A (Controls and Procedures) + PwC audit report dated 3/11/2026 + comparison to FY2024 10-K material weakness disclosures
rfm_tuples.M_value: PwC's audit report (Boston, MA, March 11, 2026) confirms material weaknesses identified and that the firm 'considered these material weaknesses in determining the nature, timing, and extent of audit tests.' These weaknesses already produced (i) a restatement of the FY2023 financials and all 2023 interim periods, (ii) restatement of 2024 interim periods, (iii) acquisition/integration cost adjustments at 12/31/2024 year-end, and (iv) 'immaterial misstatements to substantially all significant accounts and disclosures as of December 31, 2025 and 2024.' PwC has been auditor only since 2024 (i.e., new audit relationship coincides with the merger). Remediation 'is still ongoing.'
rfm_tuples.interpretation: Mode B: by the company's own admission its 12/31/2025 financial statements contain immaterial misstatements 'to substantially all significant accounts.' This is the rare case where a public-co CFO concedes the numbers are wrong but immaterial. Combined with a $1B goodwill impairment whose fair-value model PwC flagged as a critical audit matter requiring specialized professionals, the financial-reporting reliability of TTGT is impaired at the entity level. Material weaknesses persisting >18 months into the post-merger entity suggest organizational under-resourcing in finance — exactly the wrong gap for an issuer trying to demonstrate the merger thesis is intact.

rfm_tuples.claim_text: Form 4 evidence — CEO Gary Nugent open-market PURCHASED 4,200 shares at $5.85 on 2025-09-12 (~$24.5K). Director David Flaschen open-market PURCHASED 20,000 shares at $5.9662 on 2025-09-12 (~$119K). Director Michael Griffey ran a sustained open-market PURCHASE program in December 2024 of approximately 148,237 shares at $20.00-$27.00 (~$3.3M+) immediately after the merger close. No going-concern qualifier was issued; company asserts it has 'sufficient cash on hand, positive working capital, and ability to access additional cash under its Credit Facility' for next 12 months.
rfm_tuples.R: [Form 4 transactions filed 2025-09-12 to 2025-09-15] code P (open-market purchase) by CEO Gary John Nugent and Director David J S Flaschen at ~$5.85-$5.97/share
rfm_tuples.f_method: form4 m-source: parse Form 4 XML for all 36 pre-cutoff Form 4 filings; classify by code P vs S vs M/A; cross-reference with insider title and timing relative to capital events
rfm_tuples.M_value: Code-P PURCHASES by named executives/directors into the drawdown: (1) CEO Gary Nugent 4,200 sh @ $5.85 on 9/12/2025 — establishing initial direct-ownership position; (2) Director David Flaschen 20,000 sh @ $5.9662 on 9/12/2025 — likewise establishing position from zero; (3) Director Michael Griffey 148,237 sh purchased 12/3/2024-12/20/2024 at $20.00-$27.00 (~$3.3M). Cluster of director RSU/grant awards (code A) on 7/24/2025, 8/14/2025, 12/11/2025. Officer SELLS in 2025 were limited and predominantly net-settlement-related: Niemiec (CRO) sold 21,478 @ $5.75 on 8/29/2025; Noreck (CFO) sold 8,459 @ $5.99 on 8/22/2025; Tierney (CTO) sold 3,112 @ $5.99 on 8/22/2025; Rennick sold 3,498 @ $5.99 on 8/22/2025 — all aligned with 8/13/2025 RSU vesting (code M) immediately preceding, suggesting tax-related, not opportunistic distribution. Five Form 144 notices total (3 on 8/22/2025 ~$90K aggregate, 1 on 8/29/2025 $124K, 1 on 5/22/2026 $95K) — small in dollar terms.
rfm_tuples.interpretation: Form 4 evidence MODESTLY SUPPORTS management commitment. Although the dollar magnitudes are small (CEO $25K, director Flaschen $119K, director Griffey $3.3M as a much larger and earlier post-merger conviction trade), the directional signal — CEO and a director establishing initial open-market positions at $5.85-$5.97 at the bottom of the chart in a SEVERELY-impaired issuer — is the opposite of the typical SHORT-tier pattern (clustered insider sales pre-bad-news, asymmetric sell:buy ratios). Selling activity is small, tax-aligned, and explainable by RSU vesting cycles. No 10b5-1 plan adoptions in Q4-2025. This Form 4 picture does NOT corroborate a fraud/distress narrative; it argues management has skin in the game at current price.

rfm_tuples.claim_text: Q1 2026 10-Q: 'As of March 31, 2026 and December 31, 2025, Informa TechTarget had $120.1 million and $106.7 million, respectively, drawn under the Credit Facility' (related-party $250M revolver from Informa Group Holdings Ltd, maturing Dec 2, 2029, SOFR + 2.5%). Credit Facility covenants require Consolidated Total Net Leverage Ratio ≤ 3.00x and Consolidated Interest Coverage Ratio ≥ 3.00x. FY2025 cash, cash equivalents, and short-term investments totaled $40.6M. FY2025 had $311.0M financing outflow primarily from repaying $417.0M of legacy TechTarget convertible notes ($3M 2025 Notes + $414M 2026 Notes) refinanced via the parent revolver.
rfm_tuples.R: $120.1 million and $106.7 million, respectively, drawn under the Credit Facility... [covenants] Consolidated Total Net Leverage Ratio of 3.00 to 1.00 or less... Consolidated Interest Coverage Ratio of at least 3.00 to 1.00
rfm_tuples.f_method: covenant_math — given disclosed FY2025 results, test whether covenant compliance is durable; compute pro-forma leverage on adjusted EBITDA proxy from segment table
rfm_tuples.M_source: 10-Q Note on Credit Facility + 10-K cash flow + segment operating income reconciliation
rfm_tuples.M_value: Q1 2026 segment operating income $44.99M (B2D $35.3M + I&A $9.7M) before unallocated corporate / D&A / restructuring / acquisition costs. Annualized segment OI ~$180M, but TTM net loss is ~$1B GAAP and operating cash flow was only $16.3M in FY2025. Debt grew $13.4M in Q1 2026 alone ($106.7M→$120.1M). 48% of the $250M parent-related-party revolver is now drawn vs 43% at year-end. Liquidity bridge: $40.6M cash + $130M undrawn capacity = $170M = ~10.4 months of FY2025 cash burn pre-working-capital. Covenant compliance dependent on aggressive add-backs given GAAP results. The lender IS the controlling shareholder (Informa PLC), introducing related-party concentration in event-of-default cure.
rfm_tuples.interpretation: Liquidity is currently adequate but trending the wrong way: revolver utilization is increasing, cash is low ($40.6M absolute), operating cash generation is thin ($16M FY2025), and the entire $250M facility is provided by the controlling-stockholder parent (Informa Group Holdings Ltd), not a bank syndicate. Mode B: in a true distress event, an arms-length syndicate facility is generally more cure-flexible than a parent revolver, because the parent has the conflicting incentive to renegotiate ownership economics (e.g., debt-for-equity dilution). Covenant ratios with 3.0x net leverage and 3.0x interest coverage on a business that just impaired ~$1B of goodwill and produced GAAP $1B net loss means add-backs / EBITDA definitions are doing a great deal of work.

rfm_tuples.claim_text: FY2025 total revenue of $486.8M vs FY2024 of $284.9M (+71%), driven entirely by inclusion of Former TechTarget for a full year (acquired Dec 2, 2024; FY2024 contained only ~1 month of legacy TechTarget revenue). Marketing/advertising/sponsorship revenue +$182M YoY; +$158.9M attributable to Former TechTarget full-year inclusion. Q1 2026 revenue $106.0M vs Q1 2025 $103.9M (+2.1%), the first comparable quarter post-merger close.
rfm_tuples.R: Total revenues $486,791 [FY25] vs $284,897 [FY24]... The inclusion of a full year of Former TechTarget, following its acquisition in December 2024, increased marketing, advertising services, and sponsorship revenues by $158.9 million... Total revenue $106,048 [Q1 26] vs $103,887 [Q1 25]
rfm_tuples.f_method: organic_growth_decomposition — back out M&A contribution to derive same-perimeter organic growth rate
rfm_tuples.M_source: 10-K MD&A revenue reconciliation + Q1 2026 10-Q revenues table + 12/2/2024 merger close date
rfm_tuples.M_value: Q1 2026 vs Q1 2025 IS the first apples-to-apples post-merger comparable. Reported +2.1% revenue growth. Within that: marketing/advertising/sponsorship $75.5M (+4.5%); intelligence subscriptions $18.7M (-1.0%); advisory services $11.8M (-6.1%); exhibitor/attendee $93K (-56%). Subscription revenue (the recurring/predictable line) is DECLINING. The blended +2% is well below management's 7.1% U.S. enterprise IT growth narrative in Item 1.
rfm_tuples.interpretation: Mode B: management's growth thesis (Item 1 'Enterprise IT market acceleration: forecast 7.1% CAGR') is not corroborated by Q1 2026 organic growth of +2% with subscription and advisory revenue lines DECLINING. The merger thesis was that Informa Tech Digital Businesses + legacy TechTarget combined would unlock revenue synergies and accelerate growth; the first clean quarter shows decel vs market expectation. This is a forward-quarter underdelivery that the issuer has not framed as such.

rfm_tuples.claim_text: 10-K: 'In July 2025, we committed to the Restructuring Plan designed to reshape, optimize, and support the Company's financial and operational efficiency... included the net reduction of approximately 10% of the Company's colleague base.' Restructuring costs $14.7M in FY2025, $0 in FY2024. 'Our Chief Executive Officer provides services to the Company through a secondment agreement rather than being directly employed by us' (CEO Gary Nugent is a secondee from parent Informa).
rfm_tuples.R: Restructuring Plan included the net reduction of approximately 10% of the Company's colleague base... Our Chief Executive Officer provides services to the Company through a secondment agreement rather than being directly employed by us
rfm_tuples.f_method: governance_pattern — verify parent-control disclosures and conflict-of-interest framework; assess CEO economic alignment given secondment structure
rfm_tuples.M_source: 10-K Item 1A Risk Factors + Stockholders Agreement summary + CEO Form 4 ownership profile
rfm_tuples.M_value: (1) CEO Gary Nugent is seconded from Informa PLC parent (not directly employed by TTGT); (2) Informa retains consent rights over M&A, asset sales, debt issuance, security issuance, and CEO termination/appointment pursuant to Stockholders Agreement; (3) Informa is the lender on the $250M revolver; (4) Informa supplies the Data Sharing Agreement underlying TTGT's growth thesis; (5) Informa is locked up from selling its TTGT stock until 2nd anniversary of close (December 2026) — i.e., approximately 7 months from the cutoff date. Form 4 data shows CEO Nugent had ZERO direct ownership until his 9/12/2025 4,200-share open-market purchase ($24.5K).
rfm_tuples.interpretation: Mode B: the issuer is structurally a captive subsidiary with thin public float. Five layers of parent-affiliate dependency (CEO secondee, controlled-company governance, related-party debt, related-party data feed, parent lockup expiring December 2026) mean the minority public stockholders face significant agency risk. The CEO's $24.5K open-market purchase is the only direct-ownership economic alignment of the top executive — small in absolute terms. The December 2026 lockup expiry is a calendar overhang: Informa becomes free to begin reducing its position roughly 7 months after the cutoff, which is the typical pattern that triggers float overhang and discount compression.

rfm_tuples.claim_text: 10-Q Note: 'During the first quarters of 2026 and 2025, the Company identified a sustained decline in the Company's share price which it determined to be a triggering event for the purposes of testing for goodwill impairment.' Discount rates used in Q1 2026 impairment test ranged from 21.5% to 25.5%. PwC critical audit matter highlighted 'high degree of auditor judgment, subjectivity and effort' on forecasted revenue growth rates, EBITDA margins, and discount rates.
rfm_tuples.R: discount rate used in the impairment test for the reporting units ranged from 21.5% to 25.5% under both the pre- and post-reorganization assessments
rfm_tuples.f_method: discount_rate_sanity — compare 21.5-25.5% reporting-unit discount rates against typical mid-cap B2B information-services cost of capital (~10-13%) to gauge the implied risk premium the auditors required to support residual carrying values
rfm_tuples.M_value: 21.5-25.5% WACC implies a risk-adjusted cost of capital well above the ~10-13% range typical for B2B information services / digital marketing peers. This is a 'cost of equity in a near-distressed business' rate. Sensitivity disclosures show that small changes (1% in discount rate, 10% in growth rate) would have FULLY impaired remaining goodwill in multiple reporting units. Bluefin: 1.7% decrease in forecasted revenue growth rate would have impaired all remaining goodwill. Industry Dive: 10.0% decrease in growth rate would have increased impairment by $11.1M. NetLine: 6.3% decrease in growth rate would have eliminated all remaining goodwill.
rfm_tuples.interpretation: Mode B: the discount rates the auditor and management used (21.5-25.5%) are themselves an admission that the reporting units are valued as if near-distressed. Remaining goodwill ($1.1M post-Q1-2026) is one bad quarter or one model-input flex away from full write-off. This is a quantitative tell that the forensic distress is priced into the audit assumptions, even if the going-concern language hasn't been triggered.

rfm_tuples.claim_text: 10-K: '$725.5 million and $808.7 million of net intangible assets as of December 31, 2025 and 2024, respectively.' Customer relationships, developed technology and trade names from the merger ($395M + $115M + $65M = $575M Former TechTarget intangibles, 17/7/16 year useful lives). Amortization expense increased $41.8M, or 87%, in fiscal 2025.
rfm_tuples.R: $725.5 million... of net intangible assets as of December 31, 2025... Amortization expense increased $41.8 million, or 87%, in fiscal 2025 compared to fiscal 2024
rfm_tuples.f_method: long_lived_asset_pressure — given that goodwill has been ~99% impaired, test whether the $725.5M of intangibles is the next domino, and at what speed amortization will compress reported earnings
rfm_tuples.M_source: 10-K Note on Intangible Assets + 10-Q Note 6 (Intangible Assets) confirmation
rfm_tuples.M_value: Goodwill went from $973.4M to $1.1M = effectively zero. Intangibles still $725.5M = ~57% of pre-merger goodwill+intangibles aggregate. Q1 2026 10-Q confirms the Company tested long-lived assets for impairment and did NOT find one as of March 31, 2026. But: a reporting unit's intangibles can survive an impairment that wipes its goodwill if the asset-group undiscounted cash flow test (a much weaker test than fair-value-of-reporting-unit) is barely satisfied. Annual amortization is ~$90M+ run-rate, which compresses reported operating income by ~$90M/yr vs cash earnings — exactly the kind of non-cash overhang that obscures whether the post-merger entity is structurally profitable.
rfm_tuples.interpretation: Mode B: $725.5M of customer-relationship and developed-technology intangibles sit on the balance sheet after the goodwill has been written to ~zero. The asset-group impairment test (undiscounted cash flow) gives intangibles a longer life than the goodwill fair-value test, but the directional logic is the same: if reporting units cannot support fair value above carrying for goodwill purposes, the underlying intangibles are also at risk. This is a forward impairment overhang of $725M, partially offset by ~$90M/yr amortization that would also reduce future earnings drag on impairment.

form4_summary.interpretation: CEO and one independent director established INITIAL open-market positions at $5.85-$5.97 in September 2025 (post-Q2 deterioration). Director Griffey ran a $3.3M open-market accumulation in Dec 2024 immediately post-merger. Officer 2025 sales were small, RSU-tax-aligned, and net of code-M conversions. This is NOT the SHORT-tier insider pattern (no clustered pre-bad-news selling, no large 144 proposed sales, no asymmetric sell:buy ratios). Sell:buy ratio on direct open-market $$$ is approximately 1:9 (sales ~$220K vs purchases ~$3.45M).

narrative_vs_reality_gaps: Management's growth thesis is 7.1% U.S. enterprise IT CAGR; first clean post-merger quarter (Q1 2026) printed +2.1% blended revenue with subscriptions DECLINING.

Management asserts 'sufficient cash on hand, positive working capital, and ability to access additional cash under its Credit Facility'; revolver utilization climbing (43% -> 48% in one quarter), cash only $40.6M, related-party lender is the controlling shareholder.
Material weaknesses persisting >18 months post-merger and CFO/CEO concede 'immaterial misstatements to substantially all significant accounts.'
supplemental_signals.honesty_alpha_framework_note: Per the framework's honesty principle, the goodwill impairment ($931.5M FY25 + $45M Q1-26) and material-weakness disclosures are HONESTLY DISCLOSED bad news — re-detecting them is not alpha by itself. The deployable signal is the COMBINATION of (a) management commitment evidence via Form 4 PURCHASES by CEO and directors (the framework's specific Form-4 escalation case), (b) the December 2026 Informa lockup expiry calendar event ~7 months post-cutoff, and (c) the goodwill having effectively bottomed at zero (vs an issuer with $500M of goodwill left to write off, TTGT has $1.1M).

summary: TTGT is a forensically distressed, severely impaired post-merger entity ($1B+ in goodwill writedowns in 15 months wiping ~99.9% of recorded goodwill, unremediated material weaknesses, immaterial-misstatement concessions across all significant accounts), but Form 4 evidence is the OPPOSITE of the typical SHORT-tier pattern: CEO Gary Nugent and Director David Flaschen ESTABLISHED initial open-market positions in September 2025 at $5.85-$5.97, and Director Michael Griffey ran a ~$3.3M open-market PURCHASE program in December 2024 at $20-$27. 2025 insider selling was small (~$220K total), RSU-vesting-aligned, and dwarfed ~9:1 by purchases. The framework's explicit Form-4 escalation rule — 'open-market code-P purchases by C-suite or directors, sized meaningfully, into drawdown' — applies here. Liquidity is tightening (cash $40.6M, revolver 48% drawn, related-party lender) and organic growth is decelerating (+2.1% Q1 2026 with subscriptions declining), but the insider-commitment signal contradicts a pure SHORT thesis. Verdict: NEUTRAL with LONG-leaning honesty-alpha tilt — the issuer is honest about its impairments AND insiders are buying.
